title: Evaluating the Hidden Costs of Personalization in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.28833v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While Large language models (LLMs) incorporate user personalization signals to improve usability and helpfulness, they increasingly shift from providing balanced, informative responses toward optimizing for user satisfaction when conditioned on personal context such as conversation history, inferred preferences, and user profiles. Specifically, we identify three emerging risks: (1) irrelevant personalization, where models reference personal information in unnecessary contexts; (2) preference narrowing, where models reinforce informational echo chambers; and (3) sycophantic bias, where models agree excessively with user opinions. As a result, models may reference personal information in contexts where it is unnecessary, inadvertently collapse response diversity, or agree excessively with user opinions. Despite the growing use of personalization in AI assistants, there has been limited systematic evaluation of its potential side effects. T

translated_title: 评估大语言模型个性化的隐性代价
translated_abstract: 尽管大语言模型（LLMs）通过引入用户个性化信号来提升可用性和实用性，但当模型以对话历史、推断偏好和用户画像等个人上下文为条件时，正日益从提供均衡、信息丰富的回答转向以优化用户满意度为目标。具体而言，我们识别出三种新兴风险：（1）不相关的个性化，即模型在不必要的场合引用个人信息；（2）偏好窄化，即模型强化信息茧房效应；（3）谄媚性偏见，即模型过度迎合用户观点。其结果是，模型可能在不需要的上下文中引用个人信息、无意中使回答多样性坍缩，或过度赞同用户观点。尽管个性化在AI助手中的应用日益增多，但针对其潜在副作用的系统性评估仍然有限。
tldr: 本文系统评估了大语言模型个性化的隐性代价，识别出三种新兴风险：不相关的个性化、偏好窄化和谄媚性偏见，指出个性化可能损害回答的均衡性与多样性。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically evaluates the hidden costs of personalization in large language models, identifying three emerging risks—irrelevant personalization, preference narrowing, and sycophantic bias—which can undermine balanced and informative responses.
